headline: What to Know Before Building an ADU in Los Angeles
articleBody: Accessory dwelling units, or ADUs, are regulated differently from ordinary interior remodels because state law and local implementation rules shape what can be built, where it can be placed, and how it is reviewed. California’s Department of Housing and Community Development explains that ADU law is intended to streamline approvals and expand housing supply, while local jurisdictions still apply objective standards for setbacks, height, and utility connections. In Los Angeles, that means contractors need to understand both state ADU rules and city-specific permitting procedures. This matters because an ADU builder must coordinate site planning, grading, fire separation, energy code compliance, and sometimes sewer or power upgrades. The California Energy Commission also requires ADUs to meet building energy-efficiency standards, so the contractor must plan for insulation, windows, mechanical systems, and lighting that satisfy those rules. Buyers should ask whether the contractor has completed detached ADUs, garage conversions, or attached units in Los Angeles County, because each has different structural and permitting issues. A strong contractor should be able to discuss feasibility before design is finalized, including whether an existing garage can be converted, whether setbacks or easements constrain the footprint, and whether utility submetering or panel upgrades may be needed. The most useful comparison is not price alone but the contractor’s ability to manage entitlement, plan check, and construction as one coordinated process.
